For his father had long since sent ambassadors and asked for her;
and in this year she was given.
When they reached Caesarea,
then they learned secretly of the passing of the king of kings, Hulagu,
and they were unable to turn back.
And in this same year, Sultan Izz al-Din fled from the land of Constantinople.
And he sent word to the house of Berke,
because they were neighbors of that country.
And they came, snatched him away, and departed,
and behold, he is there until this day.
And in this same year, in the days of summer, a command came to Ala al-Din, Sahib al-Diwan,
that the general command over Baghdad should be his.
And shortly after, a false report came to him,
saying: "His brother, Shams al-Din, Sahib al-Diwan, has been seized at the Ordo."
Immediately, Qara Buqa, the Shahnah of Baghdad,
laid his hand on Ala al-Din and imprisoned him in his house on the 20th
of Ab,
and he sent word to his brother.
And an order came
that Ala al-Din should go and be brought with honor,
as well as Isaac, the young Armenian man,
the secretary of Qara Buqa,
and with him a certain Arab (Ma'addite),
who said: "I was brought in order to help Ala al-Din escape."
And when they reached the Ordo,
that Arab was scourged,
and he confessed: "Isaac instructed me to lie."
And they put Isaac to death, as well as the Arab.
And from here the affairs of the Christians began to be troubled.
And in the year 1577
(1577 of the Greeks?), Bunduqdar, the ruler of Egypt, sent to King Hethum of Cilicia,
and said to him
that he should submit to him and pay tribute,
and open the road to Syria and allow grain to be imported from his country.
And that king, out of fear of the Tatars, was not able to return peaceful words to him;
and for this reason that one prepared to come to Cilicia without delay.
And the king hurried to the land of the Romans to the chief of the Tatars, whose name was Nafashi (Nafji? {OCR?}),
so that he might come to his aid.
And he replied:
"Without the command of the king of kings, I am not able to come."
And while he was sending an envoy and awaiting a reply,
the Egyptian forces launched a raid on Cilicia,
while the king was away.
